page.definition_block: Welders, cutters, solderers, and brazers use heat sources such as electric arcs, flames, and lasers to join, cut, and braze metal components. They follow drawings to control penetration and distortion and ensure joint strength under loads, heat, and corrosion.

rows.label: Education Requirement
rows.value: Typically technical secondary school or technical school + special-operations certification

rows.label: Key Skills
rows.value: Arc welding, cutting, brazing, blueprint reading, testing support, safety

rows.label: Core Activities
rows.value: Joining, cutting, brazing, fitting

rows.label: Work Values
rows.value: Precision, safety, responsibility, and endurance

rows.label: Entry Requirement
rows.value: Medium: training + certification

responsibilities_block: Position and assemble components according to drawings.
Perform arc, gas, or laser welding.
Cut and fit metal components.
Braze and repair welds while controlling distortion.
Support nondestructive testing and quality inspection for defects.
Follows safety and special-operations standards.
page.work_context_block: In the morning, collect materials and review drawings and the safety briefing. Tack components, then complete root and cover passes. At midday, perform overhead welding inside a hot tank. In the afternoon, cut materials and finish only after nondestructive testing passes. Safety personnel monitor high-risk work throughout.
